title: Arakhin 33
description: Why the Jubilee was still counted after the exile of Reuben and Gad, Jeremiah’s return of the ten tribes, the houses of unwalled courtyards that have the advantages of both houses and fields, the inheritance of houses in Levite cities, the Levites’ open land, and which walls make a walled city.
topics: 🗓️ Counting Jubilee Years in Ezra’s day: certainly not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda
📜 “At the end of seven years”: Jeremiah brought back the ten tribes and Josiah ruled over them
🏡 Houses of unwalled courtyards: redeemed like houses, released in the Jubilee like fields
⚖️ Rav Huna, Rav Pappa and Rabbi Oshaya on “and they shall go out in the Jubilee”
🏘️ Two courtyards of two houses each: walled, yet like the unwalled
🧬 Inheriting from a mother’s father: Rabbi and the Rabbis on the cities of the Levites
🌾 Field, empty lot and city: in the Levites’ cities none may be changed
🧱 Which wall counts: one built by gentiles before the conquest

a1.he: הָנִיחָא לְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי: שְׁנַת חֲמִשִּׁים אֵינָהּ מִן הַמִּנְיָן, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר: שְׁנַת חֲמִשִּׁים עוֹלָה לְכָאן וּלְכָאן, לְמָה לִי? בִּשְׁמִיטִּין סַגִּיא! הָא וַדַּאי דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

a2.he: וְלֹא מָנוּ שְׁמִיטִּין וְיוֹבְלוֹת? וְהָכְתִיב: ״מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים תְּשַׁלְּחוּ אִישׁ אֶת אָחִיו הָעִבְרִי אֲשֶׁר יִמָּכֵר לְךָ״!

a3.he: וְהָוֵינַן בְּהוּ: ״מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים״? וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַעֲבָדְךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים״! וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: שֵׁשׁ לַנִּמְכָּר, וְשֶׁבַע לַנִּרְצָע.

a4.he: הָהוּא בְּתוֹכָחָה כְּתִיב, וְקָאָמַר נָבִיא: הֲשִׁלַּחְתֶּם? וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ וַיְשַׁלֵּחוּ״!

a5.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יִרְמְיָה הֶחְזִירָן, וְיֹאשִׁיָּה בֶּן אָמוֹן מָלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶן. וּמְנָא לַן דַּהֲדוּר? דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי הַמּוֹכֵר אֶל הַמִּמְכָּר לֹא יָשׁוּב״. אֶפְשָׁר יוֹבֵל בָּטֵל, וְנָבִיא מִתְנַבֵּא עָלָיו שֶׁיִּבְטַל? אֶלָּא מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶחְזִירָן יִרְמְיָה.

a6.he: וּמְנָלַן דְּיֹאשִׁיָּה מָלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶן? דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר מָה הַצִּיּוּן הַלָּז אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי רוֹאֶה, וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו אַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר הַקֶּבֶר אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר בָּא מִיהוּדָה וַיִּקְרָא אֶת הַדְּבָרִים עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בֵּית אֵל״.

a7.he: וְכִי מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ בְּבֵית אֵל? אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהֶחְזִירָן יִרְמְיָהוּ, יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ מָלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם. רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״גַּם יְהוּדָה שָׁת קָצִיר לָךְ בְּשׁוּבִי שְׁבוּת עַמִּי״.

a8.he: מַתְנִי׳ בָּתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים נוֹתְנִין לָהֶם כֹּחַ יָפֶה שֶׁבְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה וְכֹחַ יָפֶה שֶׁבַּשָּׂדוֹת, וְנִגְאָלִין מִיָּד וְכׇל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ כְּבָתִּים, וְיוֹצְאִין בַּיּוֹבֵל וּבְגִרְעוֹן כֶּסֶף כְּשָׂדוֹת.

a9.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״עַל שְׂדֵה הָאָרֶץ יֵחָשֵׁב״ — הִקִּישׁוֹ הַכָּתוּב לִשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, מָה שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה יוֹצֵא בַּיּוֹבֵל וּבְגִרְעוֹן כֶּסֶף, אַף בָּתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים יוֹצְאִין בַּיּוֹבֵל וּבְגִרְעוֹן כֶּסֶף.

a10.he: אִי מָה שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת בְּפָחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים, אַף בָּתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים אֵינָם נִגְאָלִים פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״גְּאוּלָּה תִּהְיֶה לוֹ״ — מִיָּד. הוֹאִיל וְנָתַתָּ לָהֶם כֹּחַ יָפֶה שֶׁבַּשָּׂדוֹת וְכֹחַ יָפֶה שֶׁבַּבָּתִּים, יָכוֹל לֹא יֵצְאוּ בַּיּוֹבֵל? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״.

a11.he: מַאי קָאָמַר? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְמַקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת בְּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים, וּגְאָלוֹ אַחֵר מִיַּד הֶקְדֵּשׁ, וּפָגַע בּוֹ יוֹבֵל בְּשָׁנָה שְׁנִיָּה.

a12.he: לְמַאי מְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ? אִי לְבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה מְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ — אִיחֲלֵיט לֵיהּ לְלוֹקֵחַ, אִי לִשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה מְדַמֵּית — לְכֹהֲנִים נָפְקָא, לְהָכִי אִצְטְרִיךְ ״וּבְיֹבֵל יֵצֵא״.

a13.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב זְעֵירָא: מַאי אִירְיָא גְּאָלוֹ אַחֵר? אֲפִילּוּ לֹא גְּאָלוֹ נָמֵי! אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹצֵא בְּלֹא פִּדְיוֹן.

a14.he: מְנָלַן? מִבֶּן לֵוִי — מָה בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחוֹ בְּמִמְכָּרוֹ, הוֹרַע כֹּחוֹ בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹ; יִשְׂרָאֵל — שֶׁהוֹרַע כֹּחוֹ בְּמִמְכָּרוֹ, אֵין דִּין שֶׁהוֹרַע כֹּחוֹ בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹ?

a15.he: וְהָתָם מְנָלַן? דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְיָצָא מִמְכָּר״, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ עֲבָדָיו מִטַּלְטְלָיו וּשְׁטָרָיו, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״.

a16.he: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מִמְכַּר״? מִמְכָּריוֹ יוֹצֵא בְּחִנָּם, וְאֵין הֶקְדֵּשׁ יוֹצֵא בְּחִנָּם, אֶלָּא בְּפִדְיוֹן.

a17.he: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: הַכֹּל הָיוּ בִּכְלַל ״וְנָתַן הַכֶּסֶף וְקָם לוֹ״.

a18.he: כְּשֶׁפָּרַט הַכָּתוּב בִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״ — שָׂדֶה הוּא דִּפְרַק לֵיהּ וְנָפְקָא לְכֹהֲנִים, אֲבָל הָנָךְ כִּדְקָיְימִי קָיְימִי.

a19.he: ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״, לְמָה לִי? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְמוֹכֵר בַּיִת בְּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים, וּפָגַע בּוֹ יוֹבֵל בְּשָׁנָה שְׁנִיָּה.

a20.he: לְמַאי מְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ? אִי לְבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה מְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ — אִיחֲלֵט לֵיהּ לְלוֹקֵחַ, אִי לִשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה מְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ — הַשְׁלָמָה בָּעֵי, לְהָכִי אִצְטְרִיךְ ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״.

a21.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא, וּתְיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת בְּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים — הֲרֵי זֶה גּוֹאֵל מִיָּד וְגוֹאֲלוֹ לְעוֹלָם; גְּאָלוֹ אַחֵר מִיַּד הֶקְדֵּשׁ, הִגִּיעַ יוֹבֵל וְלֹא נִגְאַל — חוֹזֵר לַבְּעָלִים בַּיּוֹבֵל.

b1.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵלּוּ הֵן בָּתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים — שְׁנֵי חֲצֵרִים שֶׁל שְׁנֵי בָתִּים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, הֲרֵי הֵן כְּבָתֵּי חֲצֵרִים.

b2.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִמַּשְׁמַע שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״בָּתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים״ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חוֹמָה? מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהֶם חוֹמָה״? אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חוֹמָה כְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חוֹמָה. וְכַמָּה? בָּתִּים — שְׁנַיִם, חֲצֵירוֹת — שְׁנַיִם, שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת שֶׁל שְׁנֵי בָתִּים.

b3.he: וְאֵימָא בַּיִת וְחָצֵר! אִם כֵּן לִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״חֲצֵרִים״, וְכִי תֵּימָא אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״חֲצֵרִים״ — חָצֵר בְּלֹא בַּיִת מַשְׁמַע, הַהוּא קַרְפֵּף אִיקְּרִי.

b4.he: מַתְנִי׳ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיָּרַשׁ אֲבִי אִמּוֹ לֵוִי — אֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל כַּסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה. וְכֵן לֵוִי שֶׁיָּרַשׁ אֶת אֲבִי אִמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל — אֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל כַּסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה.

b5.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי בָתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הִוא אֲחוּזָּתָם״, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא לֵוִי וְעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ אֲמוּרִים אֶלָּא בְּעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.

b6.he: גְּמָ׳ וְאֶלָּא כְּמַאן? כְּבֶן לֵוִי. וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: ״עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא לֵוִי וְעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם״.

b7.he: אֵימָא: אֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל אֶלָּא כַּסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא לֵוִי וְעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.

b8.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם — דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי בָּתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם״, אֶלָּא לֵוִי מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן הַלְוִיִּם״.

b9.he: תַּנְיָא: ״וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן הַלְוִיִּם״ — יָכוֹל לֵוִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יִגְאַל, שֶׁזֶּה יִפָּה כֹּחוֹ וְזֶה הוֹרַע כֹּחוֹ, אֲבָל לֵוִי מִלֵּוִי לֹא, שֶׁזֶּה יִפָּה כֹּחוֹ וְזֶה יִפָּה כֹּחוֹ — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִן הַלְוִיִּם״.

b10.he: ״מִן הַלְוִיִּם״ — וְלֹא כׇּל הַלְוִיִּם, פְּרָט לְבֶן לֵוִי מַמְזֵר וְנָתִין.

b11.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ אֲמוּרִים אֶלָּא בְּעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם. אֲבָל עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא לֵוִי — לָא אָמְרִינַן.

b12.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין עוֹשִׂין שָׂדֶה מִגְרָשׁ, וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ שָׂדֶה, וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ עִיר, וְלֹא עִיר מִגְרָשׁ.

b13.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, אֲבָל בְּעָרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין שָׂדֶה מִגְרָשׁ, וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ שָׂדֶה, מִגְרָשׁ עִיר, וְלֹא עִיר מִגְרָשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא יַחְרִיבוּ אֶת עָרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם מוֹכְרִין לְעוֹלָם, וְגוֹאֲלִין לְעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״גְּאוּלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם״.

b14.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: ״בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, אֲבָל בְּעָרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין״ וְכוּ׳. דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהָא בְּדִלְוִיִּם לָא מְשַׁנֵּינַן, מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי?

b15.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר״. מַאי ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״? אִילֵּימָא לֹא יִמָּכֵר כְּלָל, וְהָא מִדִּכְתִיב: ״גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם״, מִכְּלָל דִּמְזַבְּנִי. אֶלָּא מַאי ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״? לֹא יְשַׁנֶּה.

b16.he: הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם מוֹכְרִין לְעוֹלָם וְגוֹאֲלִין לְעוֹלָם. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר לָךְ״, יָכוֹל אַף זֶה כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״גְּאוּלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם״.

b17.he: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״, יָכוֹל אַף זֶה כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״גְּאוּלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם״.

b18.he: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר לוֹ חוֹמָה לַצְּמִיתוּת״, יָכוֹל אַף זֶה כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״גְּאוּלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם״.

b19.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי לְחַיֵּי, אֶלָּא בָּתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה לִלְוִיִּם מִי אִית לְהוּ? וְהָתַנְיָא: עָרִים הַלָּלוּ אֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן לֹא כְּפָרִים קְטַנִּים וְלֹא כְּרַכִּים גְּדוֹלִים, אֶלָּא עֲיָירוֹת בֵּינוֹנִיּוֹת!

b20.he: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן — שֶׁהוּקַּף וּלְבַסּוֹף יָשַׁב, כָּאן — שֶׁיָּשַׁב וּלְבַסּוֹף הוּקַּף.

b21.he: וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי הָוְיָא חוֹמָה? וְהָתַנְיָא: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה״ — שֶׁהוּקַּף וּלְבַסּוֹף יָשַׁב, וְלֹא שֶׁיָּשַׁב וּלְבַסּוֹף הוּקַּף.

b22.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ הִקִּיפוּהָ יִשְׂרָאֵל? נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״חוֹמָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״חוֹמָה״, מָה לְהַלָּן גּוֹיִם, אַף כָּאן גּוֹיִם.

b23.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ הִקִּיפוּהָ גּוֹיִם לְאַחַר מִכֵּן? נֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״חוֹמָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״חוֹמָה״, מָה לְהַלָּן גּוֹיִם קוֹדֶם לָכֵן, אַף כָּאן גּוֹיִם קוֹדֶם לָכֵן!

b24.he: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לָהֶן

messages.text: Continued from 32b: a baraita taught that the Jews counted Jubilee Years in the days of Ezra, though the Jubilee had been nullified since the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh were exiled. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak explained: they counted Jubilee Years in order to sanctify the Sabbatical Years.

This works out well according to the Rabbis, who say that the fiftieth year is not included in the counting of the cycle of Sabbatical Years. It was therefore necessary to count the Jubilee Year. But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says that the fiftieth year is counted for here and for there, i.e., it is both the fiftieth year of the previous cycle and the first year of the subsequent cycle, why do I need for them to count the Jubilee Years? If the Jubilee Year is not in effect, then it is enough to count the Sabbatical Years.

notes.he: דפליגי עליה דר' יהודה [דאמרי] שנת חמשים אינה ממנין השמיטין אצטריך לממני יובלות כדקאמרת:
notes.en: This works out well according to the Rabbis: who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda [and say] that the fiftieth year is not part of the count of the Sabbatical cycles. It was necessary to count Jubilee Years, as you said.

notes.dh: אלא לרבי יהודה דאמר שנת חמשים
notes.he: הויא שנת יובל ועולה נמי למנין שמיטה הבאה ל"ל לממני יובלות בשמיטין סגיא משבע לשבע שנים יעשו שמיטה לעולם שאין שנה מפסקת בנתיים ואין כאן שום טעות:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says the fiftieth year: is the Jubilee Year and also counts toward the next Sabbatical cycle, why do I need to count Jubilee Years? Counting Sabbatical Years is enough: every seven years they would always observe a Sabbatical Year, since no year interrupts between them, and there is no room for error here.

notes.he: אצטריך למימני יובלות כדי לקדש שמיטה בזמן:
notes.en: This works out well according to the Rabbis: it was necessary to count Jubilee Years in order to sanctify the Sabbatical Year at its proper time.

notes.he: דעולה נמי לכאן ולכאן ליובל ולמנות ממנה א' ב' ג' ד' עד ז':
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says: that it counts for here and for there, for the Jubilee and to count from it one, two, three, four, up to seven.

notes.he: למימני יובלות בשמיטין סגיא:
notes.en: Why do I need: to count Jubilee Years? Counting Sabbatical Years is enough.

messages.text: That baraita is certainly not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: דקתני לעיל מנו שמיטין ויובלות בימי עזרא דלא כר' יהודה:
notes.en: Certainly: what was taught above, that they counted Sabbatical and Jubilee Years in the days of Ezra, is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: דתני אף ביאתן בימי עזרא מנו יובלות דלא כרבי יהודה דלר' יהודה לא אצטריך ולא מנו שמיטין ויובלות מאחר שגלו שבט ראובן ושבט גד:
notes.en: That certainly: what was taught, that even on their arrival in the days of Ezra they counted Jubilee Years, is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, for according to Rabbi Yehuda it was not needed. [The Gemara goes on:] And did they not count Sabbatical and Jubilee Years after the tribe of Reuben and the tribe of Gad were exiled?

messages.text: And did they not count Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years once the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh were exiled? But isn’t it written that Jeremiah, who lived many years later, said: “At the end of seven years you shall let go every man his brother that is a Hebrew, that has been sold unto you, and has served you six years, you shall let him go free from you; but your fathers did not listen unto Me, nor inclined their ear”?

verse.he: מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים תְּשַׁלְּחוּ אִישׁ אֶת־אָחִיו הָעִבְרִי אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּכֵר לְךָ וַעֲבָדְךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים וְשִׁלַּחְתּוֹ חׇפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ וְלֹא־שָׁמְעוּ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם אֵלַי וְלֹא הִטּוּ אֶת־אׇזְנָם׃
verse.en: “In the seventh year each of you must let go any fellow Hebrew who may be sold to you; when they have served you six years, you must set them free.” But your ancestors would not obey Me or give ear.

notes.he: בימי סנחריב:
notes.en: And did they not count Jubilee Years: from the days of Sennacherib [who exiled the tribes]?

notes.he: בצדקיה:
notes.en: But isn’t it written: in the days of Zedekiah.

messages.text: And we discussed this verse: Why does it state: “At the end of seven years you shall let go every man”? But isn’t it written in the same verse: “And has served you six years”?

notes.dh: מקץ שבע שנים תשלחו וגו' והוינן בה מקץ שבע שנים
notes.he: משמע לאחר שבע שנים שאף שנה שביעית והא כתיב ועבדך שש שנים:
notes.en: “At the end of seven years you shall let go” etc., and we discussed it: “At the end of seven years” implies after seven years, so that the seventh year too [is served]; but isn’t it written, “and has served you six years”?

notes.he: והוינן בה מקץ שבע שנים תשלחו מקץ שש שנים תשלחו מבעי ליה לסוף שש דהיינו ועבדך שש שנים:
notes.en: And we discussed it: “At the end of seven years you shall let go”? It should have said “At the end of six years you shall let go,” at the end of six, which is “and has served you six years.”

messages.text: The verse is referring to two separate individuals. The phrase “and has served you six years” is referring to a typical Hebrew slave who was sold, who goes free after six years (see Exodus 21:2), and the phrase “at the end of seven years” is referring to a slave whose ear was pierced with an awl to extend his tenure. Such an individual remains a slave until the Jubilee Year, even if that is the following year, i.e., the end of the seventh year.

notes.he: כדכתי' (שמות כ״א:ב׳) שש שנים יעבד:
notes.en: Six for one who was sold: as it is written (Exodus 21:2): “Six years he shall serve.”

notes.he: שהנרצע אינו יוצא עד היובל ואם נרצע ופגע יובל בשנה שמינית לרציעתו יוצא ביובל. אלמא בימי צדקיה הוה יובל וצדקיהו בימי חורבן הבית דהוו כמה וכמה דורות אחר גלות סנחריב:
notes.en: And seven for one who was pierced: since the pierced slave does not go out until the Jubilee; and if he was pierced and the Jubilee fell in the eighth year from his piercing, he goes out in the Jubilee. Evidently there was a Jubilee in the days of Zedekiah, and Zedekiah lived at the time of the destruction of the Temple, many generations after the exile of Sennacherib.

notes.he: (ועבדך שש שנים) שש שנים לנמכר כדכתיב כי תקנה עבד עברי שש שנים יעבוד ובתחילת שביעית יצא לחפשי והאי דקאמר מקץ שבע שנים תשלחו היינו שבע לנרצע שדינו של נרצע לעבוד עד יובל ואם נרצע שהיו שבע שנים עד קודם ליובל דהיינו דמקץ שבע שנים יוצא ביובל אלמא דליובלות נמי הוו מנו מאחר שגלו שבט ראובן וגד:
notes.en: And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: six years for the one who was sold, as it is written, “If you buy a Hebrew slave, six years he shall serve,” and at the beginning of the seventh he goes free. And what it says, “At the end of seven years you shall let go,” is seven for the one who was pierced, for the law of a pierced slave is to serve until the Jubilee; and if he was pierced when seven years remained before the Jubilee, that is “at the end of seven years,” he goes out in the Jubilee. Evidently they also counted Jubilee Years after the tribes of Reuben and Gad were exiled.

messages.text: If so, the verse indicates that the Jubilee Year was in effect in the times of Jeremiah, even though the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh were exiled.

That verse was not stated by Jeremiah in the form of a command; rather, it is written in the form of reproof. That is, the prophet Jeremiah is saying to the Jewish people: Did you send free the pierced slaves when the Jubilee Year was observed?

notes.he: דקא מוכח להו ירמיה וקאמר להו השלחתם באותן שנים שהייתם חייבים לשלח:
notes.en: It is written in reproof: Jeremiah is rebuking them and saying to them: Did you send them free in those years when you were obligated to send them free?

notes.he: ההוא דכתיב מקץ שבע תשלחו בתוכחה כתיב דקאמר להו נביא בתמיהא דרך תוכחה השלחתם כלומר וכי קיימתם מקץ שבע שנים תשלחו:
notes.en: The tanna could say to you: what is written, “At the end of seven years you shall let go,” is written in reproof. The prophet says to them in astonishment, by way of reproof, “Did you send free?” That is to say: did you indeed fulfill “At the end of seven years you shall let go”?

messages.text: But isn’t it written there: “And they listened and let them go”? Evidently, the entire passage is referring to matters occurring in the present.

verse.he: וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ כׇל־הַשָּׂרִים וְכׇל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר־בָּאוּ בַבְּרִית לְשַׁלַּח אִישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּוֹ וְאִישׁ אֶת־שִׁפְחָתוֹ חׇפְשִׁים לְבִלְתִּי עֲבׇד־בָּם עוֹד וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ וַיְשַׁלֵּחוּ׃
verse.en: Everyone, officials and people, who had entered into the covenant agreed to set their male and female slaves free and not keep them enslaved any longer; they complied and let them go.

notes.dh: ולא היה יובל נוהג והכתיב וישמעו וישלחו
notes.he: אלמא דהוה נהיג יובל:
notes.en: And was the Jubilee not in effect? But isn’t it written, “And they listened and let them go”? Evidently the Jubilee was in effect.

messages.text: Indeed, the Jubilee Year was not in effect once the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh were exiled. But Jeremiah brought back all the exiled tribes, and Josiah, son of Amon, ruled over them.

notes.he: לשבט ראובן וגד ויאשיה מלך עליהן הילכך מנו שמיטין ויובלות:
notes.en: Rather, Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Jeremiah brought them back: the tribes of Reuben and Gad, and Josiah ruled over them; therefore they counted Sabbatical and Jubilee Years.

messages.text: And from where do we derive that Jeremiah brought them back? As it is written: “For the seller shall not return to that which he has sold” (Ezekiel 7:13). Ezekiel prophesied that there will come a time when fields will not be returned to the owners in the Jubilee Year.

verse.he: כִּי הַמֹּכֵר אֶל־הַמִּמְכָּר לֹא יָשׁוּב וְעוֹד בַּחַיִּים חַיָּתָם כִּי־חָזוֹן אֶל־כׇּל־הֲמוֹנָהּ לֹא יָשׁוּב וְאִישׁ בַּעֲוֺנוֹ חַיָּתוֹ לֹא יִתְחַזָּקוּ׃
verse.en: For the seller shall not return to what was sold so long as both parties remain among the living. For the vision concerns all her multitude, it shall not be revoked. And because of their own guilt, none shall hold fast to their life.

notes.he: בימי צדקיהו כי המוכר אל הממכר לא ישוב דקאמר להו סופכם לגלות ויהא יובל בטל ולא יחזרו שדות לבעליהן:
notes.en: As it is written: in the days of Zedekiah, “For the seller shall not return to that which he has sold.” He was telling them: In the end you will be exiled, the Jubilee will be nullified, and fields will not return to their owners.

notes.he: מדקא מתנבא נביא כי המוכר אל הממכר לא ישוב כלומר שיבטל עוד היובל כבתחלה ולא ישובו שדות לבעליהן ש"מ דהדור שבט ראובן וגד דאי ס"ד דלא הדור מה צורך לו להתנבא שיבטל יובל והלא בטל משעה שגלו שבט ראובן וגד אלא ש"מ דהדור וכשחטאו היה מוכיחן ואמר שיבטל:
notes.en: And from where do we derive that they returned? From the prophet’s prophecy, “For the seller shall not return to that which he has sold,” that is, that the Jubilee will again be nullified as at first, and fields will not return to their owners. Conclude from it that the tribes of Reuben and Gad returned: for if you should think they did not return, why would he need to prophesy that the Jubilee would be nullified? It had been nullified from the time the tribes of Reuben and Gad were exiled! Rather, conclude from it that they returned, and when they sinned he rebuked them and said it would be nullified.

messages.text: Now, is it possible that the Jubilee Year had already been nullified and yet the prophet is prophesying that it will be annulled in the future? Rather, this teaches that Jeremiah brought back the exiled tribes.

notes.he: משגלו שבט ראובן וגד ונביא מתנבא עליו וכו':
notes.en: Is it possible that the Jubilee had been nullified: from when the tribes of Reuben and Gad were exiled, and a prophet prophesies about it etc.?

notes.dh: אלא מלמד שהחזירן ירמיה ויאשיה מלך עליהם
notes.he: ותימה שהרי אחרי שהחזירן ירמיה לא עמדו בארץ קודם חורבן כ"א ל"ו שנה כדפרישית לעיל בפ"ב (ערכין דף יב:) וא"כ לא הגיעו עד היובל והיאך נוכל למצוא וישמעו וישלחו וי"ל דנוכל למצוא אותם עבדים שהיו להם קודם שגלו והא דפריך לעיל והכתיב וישמעו וישלחו עיקר הפירכא מדכתיב (ירמיהו ל״ד:י׳) וישמעו כל השרים וכל העם אשר באו בברית משמע שנכנסו בברית לשלח עבדיהם חפשים ביובל כשיגיע היובל:
notes.en: But this teaches that Jeremiah brought them back and Josiah ruled over them: This is puzzling, for after Jeremiah brought them back they remained in the land before the destruction only thirty-six years, as I explained above in chapter 2 (Arakhin 12b). If so, they did not reach a Jubilee, so how can we account for “and they listened and let them go”? One can say that we can account for it with the slaves they had before they were exiled. And as for the Gemara’s question above, “But isn’t it written: And they listened and let them go,” the main force of the question is from what is written (Jeremiah 34:10): “And all the princes and all the people who entered into the covenant listened,” which implies that they entered into a covenant to send their slaves free in the Jubilee when the Jubilee arrived.

messages.text: And from where do we derive that Josiah ruled over all the ten tribes exiled by Assyria? As it is written: “And as Josiah turned himself, then he spied the sepulchres…then he said: What monument is that which I see? And the men of the city told him: It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel” (II Kings 23:16–17).

verse.he: וַיִּפֶן יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ וַיַּרְא אֶת־הַקְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם בָּהָר וַיִּשְׁלַח וַיִּקַּח אֶת־הָעֲצָמוֹת מִן־הַקְּבָרִים וַיִּשְׂרֹף עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וַיְטַמְּאֵהוּ כִּדְבַר יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר קָרָא אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר קָרָא אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה׃ וַיֹּאמֶר מָה הַצִּיּוּן הַלָּז אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי רֹאֶה וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו אַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר הַקֶּבֶר אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר־בָּא מִיהוּדָה וַיִּקְרָא אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ עַל הַמִּזְבַּח בֵּית־אֵל׃
verse.en: Josiah turned and saw the graves that were there on the hill; and he had the bones taken out of the graves and burned on the altar. Thus he defiled it, in fulfillment of the word of GOD foretold by the agent of God who foretold these happenings. He asked, “What is the marker I see there?” And the townspeople replied, “That is the grave of the agent of God who came from Judah and foretold these things that you have done to the altar of Bethel.”

messages.text: Now, what connection does Josiah, king of Judah, have with the altar at Bethel, a city in the kingdom of Israel? Rather, this indicates that when Jeremiah brought back the ten tribes, Josiah ruled over them.

notes.dh: מה טיבו של יאשיהו בבית אל
notes.he: דהא קרא ביאשיהו כתיב כשהיה חוזר לבער עבודת כוכבים שבארץ ישראל ובית אל של מלכי ישראל היתה ויאשיהו מלך יהודה מה טיבו בה:
notes.en: What connection does Josiah have with Bethel: the verse is written about Josiah when he was going about eradicating idol worship in the Land of Israel, and Bethel belonged to the kings of Israel. What business did Josiah, king of Judah, have there?

notes.dh: ויאמר יאשיה מה הציון הלז וגו' וכי מה טיבו של יאשיה בבית אל
notes.he: והלא בית אל של מלכי ישראל היתה אלא ש"מ שהחזירן ירמיה ויאשיה מלך עליהן]:
notes.en: “And Josiah said: What monument is that” etc. And what connection does Josiah have with Bethel? Didn’t Bethel belong to the kings of Israel? Rather, conclude from it that Jeremiah brought them back and Josiah ruled over them.

messages.text: The fact that the tribes returned may be derived from here: “Also, O Judah, there is a harvest appointed for you, when I would return the captivity of My people” (Hosea 6:11). That is, when the ten tribes will return from their captivity, a king of Judah will rule over them.

verse.he: גַּם־יְהוּדָה שָׁת קָצִיר לָךְ בְּשׁוּבִי שְׁבוּת עַמִּי׃ {פ}
verse.en:
(Even Judah has reaped a harvest of you!)
When I would restore My people’s fortunes,

notes.he: קצין דנו"ן מתחלפת ברי"ש כדכתיב נבוכד נצר נבוכד ראצר:
notes.en: Katzir [harvest]: [read it as] katzin, a ruler, for nun interchanges with resh, as it is written both Nebuchadnezzar and Nebuchadrezzar.

notes.he: קציר הוא קצין שבהרבה מקומות מתחלפת נ' בר' כמו נבוכדנצר נבוכדרצר יהודה היינו יאשיה שהיה בתחלה מלך על יהודה:
notes.en: Set a harvest [katzir]: katzir is katzin, a ruler, for in many places nun interchanges with resh, as in Nebuchadnezzar and Nebuchadrezzar. Judah: that is Josiah, who at first was king over Judah.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to the houses of the unwalled courtyards mentioned in the Torah (see Leviticus 25:31), i.e., houses in villages that are not surrounded by walls, one accords them the exceptional provisions that apply to houses of walled cities and the exceptional provisions that apply to fields.

notes.he: שאין להם לעיירות חומה:
notes.en: Mishna. Houses of the courtyards: whose towns have no wall.

notes.he: כדמפרש נגאלין מיד ואין צריך להמתין שני שנים ביד הלוקח והיינו כבתים של ערי חומה:
notes.en: Exceptional provisions: as it explains, they are redeemed immediately and need not wait two years in the buyer’s possession; and this is like houses of walled cities.

notes.he: הן כפרים שאין להם חומה:
notes.en: Houses of the courtyards: these are villages that have no wall.

messages.text: Therefore, they are redeemed immediately and for the entire twelve months following the sale, like in the sale of houses of walled cities, and not like fields, which may be redeemed only after two years.

notes.dh: נותנין להם כח יפה שבבתי ערי חומה וכח יפה שבשדות
notes.he: כיצד נגאלין מיד לאחר שנמכרו ונגאלין כל י"ב חדש כבתים וזהו כח יפה שבבתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: One accords them the exceptional provisions of houses of walled cities and the exceptional provisions of fields. How so? They are redeemed immediately after they were sold, and they are redeemed throughout the twelve months, like houses; and that is the exceptional provision of houses of walled cities.

messages.text: And they leave the possession of the buyer during the Jubilee Year or with a per annum deduction from the money of the sale price, like the sale of fields. By contrast, houses of walled cities become the possession of the buyer in perpetuity after one year, and if they are redeemed within the year, one pays the full sale price.

notes.he: שמנכה לו הלוקח לפי שנים ששהו בידו כשדות דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:כ״ז) וחשב את שני ממכרו וגו':
notes.en: And with a deduction of money: the buyer deducts for him according to the years they stayed in his possession, as with fields, as it is written (Leviticus 25:27): “Then let him count the years of its sale” etc.

notes.he: בגרעון כסף שגורע לו דמי שנים שאכל הפירות]:
notes.en: With a deduction of money: he deducts for him the value of the years in which he consumed the produce.

notes.he: ויוצאין ביובל [אם לא נגאלו] כלומר שאין נחלטין ללוקח וכשנגאלין נגאלין בגרעון כסף כתורת שדות ואינן דומין לשדות שהשדות אינו רשאי לגאול אלא לאחר שתי שנים ואלו נגאלין [אפילו] מיד:
notes.en: And they go out in the Jubilee [if they were not redeemed]: that is, they do not become the buyer’s in perpetuity; and when they are redeemed, they are redeemed with a deduction of money, by the law of fields. Yet they are not like fields, for a field one may redeem only after two years, and these are redeemed [even] immediately.

messages.caption: The mishna’s comparison: what a house of an unwalled courtyard takes from the houses of walled cities and what it takes from fields.

messages.text: Gemara

The verse states: “But the houses of the courtyards that have no wall round about them shall be reckoned with the fields of the country; they may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the Jubilee.” The verse juxtaposed houses of unwalled courtyards to an ancestral field: Just as an ancestral field leaves the possession of the buyer in the Jubilee Year or with a per annum deduction from the money of the sale price, so too, houses of the unwalled courtyards leave the possession of the buyer in the Jubilee Year or with the per annum deduction from the money of the sale price.
messages.quote: And they leave the possession of the buyer during the Jubilee Year or with a per annum deduction

verse.he: וּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים אֲשֶׁר אֵין־לָהֶם חֹמָה סָבִיב עַל־שְׂדֵה הָאָרֶץ יֵחָשֵׁב גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה־לּוֹ וּבַיֹּבֵל יֵצֵא׃
verse.en: But houses in villages that have no encircling walls shall be classed as open country: they may be redeemed, and they shall be released through the jubilee.

notes.he: בבתי החצרים כתיב:
notes.en: Gemara. “Shall be reckoned with the fields of the country”: this is written about houses of the courtyards.

notes.he: אם בא לגאלם קודם היובל:
notes.en: And with a deduction of money: if he comes to redeem them before the Jubilee.

messages.text: If one derives the halakha from an ancestral field, then just as an ancestral field may not be redeemed less than two years after its sale, so too, houses of the unwalled courtyards may not be redeemed less than two years after their sale. Therefore, the verse states: “They may be redeemed,” indicating that they may be redeemed immediately.

notes.he: כדין בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: The verse states: “They may be redeemed,” immediately: like the law of houses of walled cities.

messages.text: Since you have accorded houses of the unwalled courtyards the exceptional provisions that apply to fields and the exceptional provisions that apply to the houses of walled cities, one might have thought that they do not leave the possession of the buyer in the Jubilee Year. Therefore, the verse states: “And they shall go out in the Jubilee.”

What is the tanna of the baraita saying in the last clause, i.e., why might one think that such houses do not leave the possession of the buyer in the Jubilee Year? After all, ancestral fields leave the possession of the buyer in the Jubilee Year, and the tanna teaches that the exceptional provisions of an ancestral field apply to houses in unwalled courtyards.
messages.quote: one might have thought that they do not leave the possession of the buyer in the Jubilee Year

notes.he: מהיכא תיתי דלא יצאו ביובל הלא הוקשו לשדה אחוזה ולמאי אצטריך וביובל יצא:
notes.en: What is it saying: where would one get the idea that they do not go out in the Jubilee? They were juxtaposed to an ancestral field! So what was “and they shall go out in the Jubilee” needed for?

notes.he: אדרבה כיון דיפה כוחן דינם שיצאו ביובל:
notes.en: [One might have thought that they do not go out in the Jubilee.] What is it saying? On the contrary: since their power is enhanced, their law is that they go out in the Jubilee.

messages.text: The verse is necessary only for the case of one who consecrates a house among the houses of the unwalled courtyards, and another redeemed it from the possession of the Temple treasury, and the Jubilee Year arrived in the second year after its redemption.

notes.he: ללקיחתו של זה שלקחה מן הגזבר:
notes.en: And the Jubilee arrived in the second year: of the purchase by this one, who bought it from the treasurer.

notes.he: שגאלו:
notes.en: And the Jubilee arrived in the second year: after he redeemed it.

messages.text: To what will you compare this case? If you compare this house to houses of walled cities that were consecrated and redeemed by another, then the house belongs to the buyer in perpetuity by the end of the first year (see 31b). If you compare it to an ancestral field that was consecrated and redeemed by another, it leaves to the possession of the priests in the Jubilee Year (see 25a).

notes.he: דהכי תניא לעיל גאלה אחר מיד הקדש הגיע היובל ולא נגאלה היה חלוט לו:
notes.en: It belongs to the buyer [in perpetuity]: for so it was taught above: if another redeemed it from the Temple treasury, the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed, it is his in perpetuity.

notes.he: דהמקדיש שדה אחוזה וגאלה אחר יוצאה לכהנים ביובל. ולהכי נקט שנה שניה דאי פגע בשנה ראשונה לא אצטריך וביובל יצא דכי מדמית ליה לבתי ערי חומה אכתי לא איחלט ליה ונפיק ביובל דהא יש לו כח יפה שבשדות:
notes.en: It goes out to the priests: for one who consecrates an ancestral field and another redeemed it, it goes out to the priests in the Jubilee. And that is why he specified the second year: had the Jubilee arrived in the first year, “and they shall go out in the Jubilee” would not be needed, for even if you compare it to houses of walled cities it has not yet become his in perpetuity, and it goes out in the Jubilee, since it has the exceptional provision of fields.

notes.he: האי בית:
notes.en: To what will you compare it: this house.

notes.dh: אי לבתי ערי חומה מדמית ליה איחלט ליה ללוקח
notes.he: זה שגאלה מיד הקדש שהרי הוחלטה לו לאחר י"ב חדש כדאמרן לעיל גאלה אחר מיד הקדש הגיע יום י"ב חדש ולא נגאלה היה חלוט לו:
notes.en: If you compare it to houses of walled cities, it becomes the buyer’s in perpetuity: this one who redeemed it from the Temple treasury, for it became his in perpetuity after twelve months, as we said above: if another redeemed it from the Temple treasury and the twelve months came to an end and it was not redeemed, it is his in perpetuity.

notes.dh: ואי לשדה אחוזה מדמית ליה לכהנים נפקא
notes.he: שהרי גאלה אחר וכדאמרינן בפרקין דלעיל ואם מכרה גזבר לאחר לא יגאל אלא יוצאת לכהנים דכתיב והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל לכהן תהיה:
notes.en: And if you compare it to an ancestral field, it goes out to the priests: since another redeemed it, as we say in the previous chapter: if the treasurer sold it to another, it is not redeemed, but goes out to the priests, as it is written: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee…shall be for the priest.”

messages.text: For this reason it was necessary for the verse to state: “And they shall go out in the Jubilee,” to teach that houses in unwalled courtyards which were consecrated and redeemed by another are returned to their owners in the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: דהדרא לבעלים:
notes.en: For this reason it was necessary, “and they shall go out in the Jubilee”: that it returns to the owners.

messages.text: Why is it necessary to interpret this verse as referring specifically to a case where another redeemed the house from the Temple treasury? Even if another did not redeem it, the house should also be returned to its owner in the Jubilee Year, as the verse states simply: “And they shall go out in the Jubilee.”
messages.quote: and another redeemed it from the possession of the Temple treasury

notes.he: אחר נמי ליפוק מיד הקדש דהא כתיב וביובל יצא דלא אצטריך למכתב משום מכר הדיוט דהא אתקש לשדות:
notes.en: Even if he did not redeem it: [if no] other [redeemed it], let it also leave the Temple treasury’s possession, since it is written “and they shall go out in the Jubilee,” which was not needed for an ordinary sale, since they were already juxtaposed to fields.

notes.he: יוצא לבעלים אם הקדישן דהא כתיב וביובל יצא]:
notes.en: Even if another did not redeem it: if they consecrated it, it should also go out to the owners, since it is written “and they shall go out in the Jubilee.”

messages.text: @Rav Zeira An unredeemed house is not returned to its owners in the Jubilee Year, so that people will not say that consecrated property can leave the possession of the Temple treasury without redemption.

notes.he: אם לא גאלה אחר אינה יוצאה לו גזירה שלא יאמרו [הקדש יוצא בלא פדיון]:
notes.en: Abaye said to him: if another did not redeem it, it does not go out to him. [It is] a decree, so that people will not say [consecrated property goes out without redemption].

messages.text: And from where do we derive that consecrated property does not leave the possession of the Temple treasury without redemption? We derive it from the halakha with regard to a Levite:

notes.he: שגואל מיד שדה מגרש עריהם ובתי ערי חומה גואלין לעולם ויוצאין ביובל כדאמר לקמן:
notes.en: A Levite, whose power is enhanced with regard to his sale: in that he redeems a field of the open land of their cities immediately, and their houses of walled cities they may redeem forever, and they go out in the Jubilee, as is stated below.

messages.text: And what, if with regard to a Levite, whose power is enhanced with regard to his sale, as a Levite may always redeem a field or house that he sold (see mishna in 33b), his power is diminished with regard to his consecration, as a field that he consecrated does not leave the possession of the Temple treasury until he redeems it; then with regard to an Israelite, whose power is diminished with regard to his sale, since if he sells an ancestral field he may not redeem it for the first two years, and he may redeem a house of a walled city only within one year of the sale, is it not logical that his power is diminished with regard to his consecration and that if he consecrated a house of an unwalled courtyard he must redeem it from the Temple treasury before it enters his possession?

notes.he: שלא יוצא בלא פדיון כדמפרש לקמן:
notes.en: His power is diminished with regard to his consecration: in that it does not go out without redemption, as is explained below.

notes.he: דאינה יוצאה בלא פדיון מבן לוי [שיפה כוחו בממכרו כדתנן לקמן הכהנים והלוים מוכרין לעולם וגואלין לעולם הורע כוחו בהקדשו כדאמרינן לקמן דאינו יוצא בלא פדיון ישראל שהורע כוחו בממכרו שאינו גואל אלא לאחר ב' שנים]:
notes.en: And from where do we derive: that it does not go out without redemption? From a Levite, [whose power is enhanced with regard to his sale, as we learn below: the priests and the Levites sell always and redeem always; his power is diminished with regard to his consecration, as we say below that it does not go out without redemption. An Israelite, whose power is diminished with regard to his sale, in that he redeems only after two years.]

messages.text: And there, with regard to a Levite, from where do we derive that his consecrated property does not leave the possession of the Temple treasury without redemption?

notes.he: דאין הקדשו של בן לוי יוצא בלא פדיון:
notes.en: And there, from where do we derive: that a Levite’s consecrated property does not go out without redemption?

messages.text: With regard to the verse: “And if a man purchases from the Levites, the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall go out during the Jubilee Year”: from the phrase “that was sold…shall go out” I would derive that any item sold by a Levite returns to him in the Jubilee Year, even his slaves, movable property, and promissory notes. Therefore, the verse states: “House…in the city of his possession,” which teaches that these items do not return to the Levite without redemption.

verse.he: וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן־הַלְוִיִּם וְיָצָא מִמְכַּר־בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ בַּיֹּבֵל כִּי בָתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הִוא אֲחֻזָּתָם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en: Such property as may be redeemed from Levi—houses sold in a city it holds—shall be released through the jubilee; for the houses in the cities of Levi are its holding among the Israelites.

notes.he: אי הוה כתיב ואשר יגאל מן הלוים ויצא ממכר ביובל ולא הוה כתב בית הוה אמינא אפילו שטרי ומטלטלין של לוי אם מכרן יוצאין לו ביובל:
notes.en: “That was sold…shall go out”: had it been written “And if a man purchases from the Levites, that was sold shall go out in the Jubilee,” without writing “house,” I would have said that even a Levite’s promissory notes and movable property, if he sold them, return to him in the Jubilee.

notes.he: דתניא ואשר יגאל [מן הלוים] ויצא ממכר בית ועיר אחוזתו ביובל:
notes.en: As it is taught: “And if a man purchases [from the Levites], the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall go out in the Jubilee.”

notes.he: שאפילו מכר עבדיו ושטריו ומטלטליו שחוזרין ביובל]:
notes.en: [I would understand: that even if he sold his slaves, his promissory notes and his movable property, they return in the Jubilee.]

notes.he: ת"ל בית ועיר [אחוזתו] שהן קרקע למעוטי הני:
notes.en: The verse states: “House…in the city [of his possession],” which are land, to exclude these.

messages.text: What is the meaning when the verse states: “That was sold”? The verse teaches that a house or field that was sold by a Levite leaves the possession of the buyer and enters the Levite’s possession for free in the Jubilee Year, but the consecration of a Levite does not leave for free in the Jubilee Year; rather, it leaves only with redemption.

notes.dh: א"כ מה ת"ל ממכרו דמשמע כל ממכר
notes.he: לא להכי כתב ממכר דממכרו [של קרקע] יוצא [בחנם] ביובל (אבל הקדישו אפילו קרקע אין) [ואין הקדשו] יוצא בחנם אלא בפדיון וכ"ש הקדשו של ישראל שאינו יוצא מהקדש בלא פדיון:
notes.en: If so, what does the verse teach by “that was sold,” which implies any sale? It wrote “that was sold” for this: his sale [of land] goes out [for free] in the Jubilee, [but his consecration does not] go out for free, only with redemption; and all the more so an Israelite’s consecration does not leave the Temple treasury without redemption. [The text carries an older bracketed reading of the middle phrase.]

messages.text: And Rav Huna, who says that a house in an unwalled courtyard that was consecrated and subsequently redeemed by another returns to the original owner in the Jubilee Year, disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya.
messages.quote: one who consecrates a house among the houses of the unwalled courtyards, and another redeemed it

notes.he: הא דאמר רב הונא לעיל מקדיש בית בבתי חצרים וגאלה אחר מיד הקדש יוצאה מידו וחוזרת לבעלים ביובל פליגא אדרבי אושעיא:
notes.en: And disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya: what Rav Huna said above, that if one consecrates a house among the houses of the courtyards and another redeemed it from the Temple treasury, it leaves his possession and returns to the owners in the Jubilee, disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya.

messages.text: All items were included in the command: And he will give the money and it will be assured to him (see Leviticus 27:19), i.e., one who redeems an item from the Temple treasury becomes its owner in all regards.

notes.he: שהלוקח כלום מיד הקדש יקום המקח בידו לעולם:
notes.en: Within “And he will give the money and it will be assured to him”: that whatever one buys from the Temple treasury, the purchase stands in his possession forever.

notes.he: [והאי דקאמר רב הונא דמקדיש בית בבתי ערי חצרים וגאלו אחר מיד הקדש דיוצא מידו ביובל וחוזרת לבעלים. והיינו פליגא דר' אושעיא דאמר ר' אושעיא] הכל היו בכלל ונתן הכסף וקם לו. בין מקדיש ביתו בין מקדיש שדה אחוזתו בין מקדיש בית בבתי ערי חומה בין בבתי חצרים שהוא של פודה ואינו יוצא מידו ביובל:
notes.en: [And what Rav Huna says, that if one consecrates a house among the houses of unwalled courtyards and another redeemed it from the Temple treasury, it leaves his possession in the Jubilee and returns to the owners, this disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya, for Rabbi Oshaya said:] All were included in “And he will give the money and it will be assured to him”: whether one consecrates his house or his ancestral field, or a house among the houses of walled cities or among the houses of courtyards, it belongs to the redeemer and does not leave his possession in the Jubilee.

messages.text: When the verse specified with regard to an ancestral field: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy unto the Lord, as a field dedicated; his ancestral field shall be for the priest,” one derives that it is only with regard to a field that one can redeem it and yet it leaves the possession of the Temple treasury to enter the possession of the priests in the Jubilee Year. But with regard to these houses in unwalled courtyards that were consecrated and redeemed by another, they remain in their current state, i.e., in the possession of the one who redeemed them.

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: בגואל שדה אחוזה של אחרים מיד הקדש דיוצאה מידו ומתחלקת האי הוא דאפקיה רחמנא בהדיא מכלל ונתן הכסף וקם לו:
notes.en: When the verse specified: regarding one who redeems another’s ancestral field from the Temple treasury, that it leaves his possession and is divided [among the priests]: that is the one the Merciful One explicitly took out of the general rule of “and he will give the money and it will be assured to him.”

notes.he: בתי החצרים כדקיימי קיימי בכלל וקם לו ולא נפקא מידא דלוקח:
notes.en: But these: the houses of the courtyards stay as they are, within “it will be assured to him,” and do not leave the buyer’s possession.

notes.he: בגואל שדה אחוזה מיד הקדש והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל לכהן תהיה שדה הוא דפריק לה אחר ונפקא לכהנים ביובל]:
notes.en: [When the verse specified: regarding one who redeems an ancestral field from the Temple treasury, “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee…shall be for the priest”: it is a field that another redeems and it goes out to the priests in the Jubilee.]

notes.he: גואל בתי חצרים מיד הקדש:
notes.en: But all these: one who redeems houses of courtyards from the Temple treasury.

notes.he: ואינו יוצא מידו ביובל והיינו פלוגתא דרב הונא:
notes.en: Stay as they are: it does not leave his possession in the Jubilee. And this is the dispute with Rav Huna.

messages.text: According to Rabbi Oshaya, why do I need the phrase “and they shall go out in the Jubilee”?

notes.he: לרבי אושעיא ל"ל:
notes.en: “And they shall go out in the Jubilee”: according to Rabbi Oshaya, why do I need it?

notes.he: [אלא לר' אושעיא וביובל יצא דבתי חצרים למה לי:
notes.en: [But according to Rabbi Oshaya, why do I need “and they shall go out in the Jubilee” of houses of courtyards?]

messages.text: It is necessary only for the case of one who sells a house among the houses of the unwalled courtyards and the Jubilee Year arrived in the second year. The verse indicates that the house is nevertheless returned to the seller.

To what will you compare this case? If you compare this case to one of the houses of walled cities that was sold, then the house belongs to the buyer in perpetuity at the end of the first year. And if you compare it to the case of an ancestral field that was sold, then it requires completion of another year after the Jubilee Year, as taught in a baraita cited earlier (29b): If the buyer consumed an ancestral field’s produce for one year before the Jubilee Year, he completes another year after the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: להשלים לו שנה אחת משתי שנים שהיא ראויה לשהות ביד לוקח כדתניא לעיל בריש פירקין אכלה שנה אחת לפני היובל משלימין לו שנה אחרת לאחר היובל:
notes.en: It requires completion: to complete for him one year of the two years it is fit to remain in the buyer’s possession, as taught above at the beginning of our chapter: if he consumed it for one year before the Jubilee, they complete for him another year after the Jubilee.

notes.dh: לא נצרכה האי וביובל יצא אלא למוכר בית בבתי חצרים ופגע בו יובל כו'
notes.he: אי לשדה אחוזה מדמית ליה] השלמה בעי. [כדתניא בריש פירקין אכלה שנה לפני יובל משלימין לו שנה אחרת לאחר היובל]. וסד"א דלא ליפוק ביובל אלא משלימין לו להכי אצטריך וביובל יצא דאין משלימין לו:
notes.en: “And they shall go out in the Jubilee” is needed only for one who sells a house among the houses of courtyards, and the Jubilee arrived etc. [If you compare it to an ancestral field,] it requires completion: [as taught at the beginning of our chapter: if he consumed it for one year before the Jubilee, they complete for him another year after the Jubilee.] It might enter your mind that it does not go out in the Jubilee but that they complete the year for him; therefore “and they shall go out in the Jubilee” was needed, [to teach] that they do not complete it for him.

messages.text: For this reason it was necessary for the verse to state: “And they shall go out in the Jubilee,” to teach that in such a case the house of an unwalled courtyard returns to the possession of the original owner.
✖ It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rav Huna, and this baraita is a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rabbi Oshaya:

With regard to one who consecrates a house among the houses of unwalled courtyards, this individual may redeem the house immediately and he may redeem it always. If another individual redeemed it from the possession of the Temple treasury, and the Jubilee Year arrived and it was not redeemed by the original owner, the house returns to the owner in the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: תניא כוותיה דרב הונא גרסינן. כרב הונא דאמר לעיל מקדיש בית בבתי החצרים וגאלה אחר מיד מקדיש יוצאה לבעלים ביובל:
notes.en: We read: “It is taught in accordance with Rav Huna.” In accordance with Rav Huna, who said above that if one consecrates a house among the houses of the courtyards and another redeemed it from the Temple [Rashi’s text reads “from the consecrator”], it goes out to the owners in the Jubilee.

notes.he: דאמר כדקיימי קיימי בידא דלוקח:
notes.en: And a refutation of Rabbi Oshaya: who said they stay as they are, in the buyer’s possession.

notes.he: ואפילו גאלה אחר גואלה מידו ולא הויא כשדה אחוזה דכתיב בה לא יגאל עוד:
notes.en: And he may redeem it always: even if another redeemed it, he redeems it from him; it is not like an ancestral field, about which it is written (Leviticus 27:20): “It shall not be redeemed any more.”

notes.dh: גאלה אחר מיד הקדש והגיע יובל ולא גאלה
notes.he: מקדיש מידו חוזרת לו בחנם:
notes.en: If another redeemed it from the Temple treasury and the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed: by the consecrator from him, it returns to him for free.

notes.he: כדקאמר גאלו אחר מיד הקדש הגיע יובל ולא נגאל דחוזר לבעלים ביובל. היינו תיובתא דרבי אושעיא דאיהו קאמר אבל הנך כדקיימי קיימי דלא הדרי ביובל:
notes.en: [It is taught] in accordance with Rav Huna: as he said, if another redeemed it from the Temple treasury, the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed, it returns to the owners in the Jubilee. This is the refutation of Rabbi Oshaya, for he says, “but these stay as they are,” that they do not return in the Jubilee.

messages.caption: Why the verse needs “and they shall go out in the Jubilee”: Rav Huna’s case and Rav Pappa’s, and what each comparison would have produced.

messages.text: Mishna

And these are the houses of the unwalled courtyards whose halakha was taught in the previous mishna: Any city in which there are two courtyards each containing two houses, although it is surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun, their halakhic status is like that of the houses of the unwalled courtyards.

notes.he: עיר שאין בה אלא שתי חצירות:
notes.en: Mishna. Two courtyards: a town that has only two courtyards.

notes.he: שיש להן דין זה:
notes.en: And these are the houses of the courtyards: that have this law.

notes.dh: שתי חצרות של [ב'] ב' בתים אף על פי שמוקפות
notes.he: דינן כבתי חצרים ככפרים שאין להם חומה אבל פחות מיכן אינן כבתי חצרות:
notes.en: Two courtyards of [two] houses each, even though they are surrounded [by a wall]: their law is like houses of the courtyards, like villages that have no wall; but fewer than this, they are not like houses of the courtyards. [A gloss in the printed edition: it seems the tanna means to exclude more than this, which would not be like houses of courtyards; perhaps this is a scribal error and it should read “but more than this.” This requires study.]

messages.text: Gemara

By inference from that which is stated: “The houses of the courtyards,” do I not know that they have no wall around them? If so, what is the meaning when the verse states: “Which have no wall”? It means that there are certain places that even though they have a wall, they are considered like places that do not have a wall.

verse.he: וּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים אֲשֶׁר אֵין־לָהֶם חֹמָה סָבִיב עַל־שְׂדֵה הָאָרֶץ יֵחָשֵׁב גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה־לּוֹ וּבַיֹּבֵל יֵצֵא׃
verse.en: But houses in villages that have no encircling walls shall be classed as open country: they may be redeemed, and they shall be released through the jubilee.

notes.dh: גמ' איני יודע שאין להן חומה
notes.he: דבתי החצרים משמע שאינו בעיר אלא יישוב חצירות הסמוכות:
notes.en: Gemara. Do I not know that they have no wall: for “houses of the courtyards” implies that it is not a town but a settlement of adjacent courtyards.

notes.he: הואיל ואין בה כדי עיר:
notes.en: Like those that have no wall: since it does not amount to a town.

notes.he: משמע כפרים שאין להם חומה:
notes.en: Houses of the courtyards: implies villages that have no wall.

notes.he: [מה ת"ל שאין להם חומה שאע"פ שיש להם חומה מוקפות מימות יהושע כמי שאין להם חומה דמו שאינן בתורת בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: [What does the verse teach by “which have no wall”? That even though they have a wall surrounding them from the days of Joshua, they are as if they have no wall, for they are not under the law of houses of walled cities.]

messages.text: And how many, i.e., what is considered such a place? The term “houses” indicates a minimum of two, and the term “courtyards” likewise indicates a minimum of two. Therefore, if a city has only two courtyards each containing two houses, its houses are considered like the houses of the unwalled courtyards.

notes.he: הן דלא ליחשוב חומה דידהו כעיר חומה שתי חצרות וכו':
notes.en: And how many: are they, that their wall should not be counted as that of a walled town? Two courtyards etc.

messages.text: But you can say that the phrase: Houses of the courtyards, means one house and one courtyard, i.e., one house in each courtyard. Consequently, if each courtyard contains two houses, the city should be considered like a walled city.

notes.he: אבל אי איכא שני בתים בכל חצר הוו כעיר חומה ולא הוו כבתי החצרים:
notes.en: Say a house and a courtyard, a house and a courtyard: but if there are two houses in each courtyard, they are like a walled city and not like the houses of the courtyards.

notes.he: דהיינו ב' בתים וב' חצרות ולא שיהו ב' בתים בכל חצר:
notes.en: And say a house and a courtyard, a house and a courtyard: that is, two houses and two courtyards, and not that there be two houses in each courtyard.

messages.text: If so, let the Merciful One write: “Courtyards,” without mentioning houses, as a courtyard must contain at least one house.

notes.he: ולא ליכתוב בתי ואנא ידענא דאין חצר בלא בית:
notes.en: If so, let it write “courtyards”: and not write “houses,” and I would know that there is no courtyard without a house.

notes.he: דבית אחד בלבד בכל חצר:
notes.en: If so: that there is only one house in each courtyard.

notes.he: חצרים ולא בעי למכתב בתי דסתם חצר אינה בלא בית אחד:
notes.en: Let it write: “courtyards,” and there would be no need to write “houses,” for an ordinary courtyard is not without one house.

messages.text: And if you would say: If the Merciful One had written only: “Courtyards,” then one might mistakenly have concluded that the verse indicates a courtyard without a house and that if the courtyard contains a house then the city is considered walled, one could not have arrived at that conclusion, since such an area is called an enclosure [karpef], not a courtyard.

notes.he: לא ההוא חצר שאין בו בית לא מקרי חצר אלא קרפף ומדאצטריך למיכתב בתי וחצרים ש"מ דב' חצרות של ב' ב' בתים:
notes.en: No: a courtyard that has no house is not called a courtyard but a karpef [enclosure]. And since it was necessary to write “houses” and “courtyards,” conclude from it: two courtyards of two houses each.

messages.text: Mishna

An Israelite who inherited a house in a walled city from his mother’s father who was a Levite does not redeem the house in accordance with this procedure delineated in the previous mishnayot; rather, if he sold the inherited house, he may redeem it always, like a Levite. And likewise, a Levite who inherited a house in a walled city from his mother’s father who was an Israelite does not redeem the house in accordance with this procedure delineated in the previous mishnayot.

notes.he: בתי ערי חומה מאבי אמו לוי אינו גואל כסדר הזה שאם מכרה שתהא נחלטת ללוקח לסוף שנה אלא לעולם גואלה כלוי דכתיב בהו (ויקרא כ״ה:ל״ב) גאולת עולם תהיה ללוים:
notes.en: Mishna. An Israelite who inherited: houses of a walled city from his mother’s father, a Levite, does not redeem according to this procedure, that if he sold it, it becomes the buyer’s in perpetuity at the end of a year; rather, he may always redeem it, like a Levite, as it is written about them (Leviticus 25:32): “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption.”

notes.dh: ישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי] אינו גואל כסדר הזה
notes.he: כענין שאר ישראל היורשין קרוביהן ישראל (אלא דינו כבן לוי וכן בן לוי כו') [לפי שהלוים אינן בתורת מוכר שדה אחוזה לב' שנים ולא בתורת בתי ערי חומה לחלוט. וכן בתורת חצרים שנאמר כי בתי ערי הלוים היא אחוזתם עד שיהא לוי וערי הלוים משמע השתא דבין ישראל שירש אבי אמו לוי ובין לוי שירש אבי אמו ישראל גואלין בתורת ישראל ולעולם אינו גואל בסדר לוי שמוכר וגואל לעולם עד שיהא לוי ובערי הלוים]:
notes.en: [An Israelite who inherited from his mother’s father, a Levite,] does not redeem according to this procedure: like other Israelites who inherit from their Israelite relatives (but his law is like a Levite’s, and likewise a Levite etc.). [For the Levites are not under the law of one who sells an ancestral field for two years, nor under the law of houses of walled cities that become the buyer’s in perpetuity, nor likewise under the law of courtyards, as it is stated: “as the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession,” unless he is a Levite and in the cities of the Levites. It now implies that both an Israelite who inherited from his mother’s father, a Levite, and a Levite who inherited from his mother’s father, an Israelite, redeem under the law of an Israelite, and never redeem by the order of a Levite, who sells always and redeems always, unless he is a Levite and in the cities of the Levites.]

messages.text: As it is stated: “And if a man purchases from the Levites, the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall go out during the Jubilee Year; as the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.” The verse indicates that the ability to always redeem the house of a Levite does not apply unless the one selling the house will be a Levite and the house is located in the cities of the Levites. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

verse.he: וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן־הַלְוִיִּם וְיָצָא מִמְכַּר־בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ בַּיֹּבֵל כִּי בָתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הִוא אֲחֻזָּתָם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en: Such property as may be redeemed from Levi—houses sold in a city it holds—shall be released through the jubilee; for the houses in the cities of Levi are its holding among the Israelites.

notes.he: הוא המוכר לוי לאפוקי ישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי דאינו גואל כלוי:
notes.en: Unless he is: the seller is a Levite; to exclude an Israelite who inherited from his mother’s father, a Levite, who does not redeem like a Levite.

notes.he: מערים שניתנו ללוים בימי יהושע לאפוקי בן לוי שירש את אבי אמו ישראל דאינו גואל כלוי. והשתא קשיא רישא לסיפא ובגמ' מתרץ לה:
notes.en: And the cities of the Levites: of the cities given to the Levites in the days of Joshua; to exclude a Levite who inherited from his mother’s father, an Israelite, who does not redeem like a Levite. And now the first clause [of the mishna] contradicts the last, and the Gemara resolves it.

messages.text: These matters are stated only with regard to a house in the cities of the Levites, even if the owner was not a Levite.

notes.he: דגאולת עולם אמורים אלא בערי הלוים אבל עד שיהא לוי לא בעינן דישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי מודו רבנן דגואל כלוי הואיל ומערי הלוים היא זו אבל בבן לוי שירש את אבי אמו ישראל מודו רבנן דאינו גואל כלוי דבערי הלוים תלא רחמנא:
notes.en: These matters are not: [the matters of] a perpetual right of redemption are stated only regarding the cities of the Levites, but we do not require that he be a Levite. With an Israelite who inherited from his mother’s father, a Levite, the Rabbis concede that he redeems like a Levite, since this is of the cities of the Levites; but with a Levite who inherited from his mother’s father, an Israelite, the Rabbis concede that he does not redeem like a Levite, for the Merciful One made it depend on the cities of the Levites.

notes.dh: וחכ"א אין דברים הללו אמורין אלא בערי הלוים
notes.he: [משמע] דחכמים סברי דאפילו ישראל שירש ערי הלוים מוכר וגואל כתורת לוים דבערי הלוים תלא רחמנא. אבל בהא פליגי דעד שיהא לוי לא אמרינן:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: These matters are stated only in the cities of the Levites: [this implies] that the Rabbis hold that even an Israelite who inherited in the cities of the Levites sells and redeems by the law of the Levites, for the Merciful One made it depend on the cities of the Levites. And in this they disagree: we do not say “unless he is a Levite.”

messages.text: Gemara

Rather, like whom does he redeem it? He redeems it like a Levite. But Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi then teaches that the ability to always redeem the house of a Levite does not apply unless the one selling the house will be a Levite and the house is located in the cities of the Levites. If so, an Israelite who inherited a house in a walled city from his mother’s father who is a Levite should redeem it in the manner of an Israelite.
messages.quote: An Israelite who inherited a house in a walled city from his mother’s father who was a Levite does not redeem the house in accordance with this procedure

notes.he: גמ' וקא פריך אינו גואל כסדר הזה כישראל אלא כמאן כבן לוי בתמיה והא תני סיפא עד שיהא לוי כו':
notes.en: Gemara. And it asks: “He does not redeem according to this procedure” of an Israelite; rather, like whom? Like a Levite? [Asked in astonishment.] But the last clause teaches, “unless he is a Levite” etc.

messages.text: Say that the mishna means that an Israelite who inherited a house in a walled city from his mother’s father who was a Levite redeems that house only in accordance with this procedure delineated in the previous mishnayot, i.e., he has only one year to redeem it, after which the house becomes the possession of the buyer in perpetuity. And this is always the halakha unless the one selling the house will be a Levite and the house is located in the cities of the Levites, in which case he can always redeem it. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

notes.he: והא תני עד שיהא לוי וערי לוים כלומר דמי שהוא לוי ובערי לוים הוא גואל בתורת לוי ולא ישראל בערי לוים גואל כבן לוי]. אלא אימא אינו גואל אלא כסדר הזה. שאמרנו למעלה בתורת ישראל בערי ישראל:
notes.en: [Rather, like whom? Like a Levite? But it teaches “unless he is a Levite and the cities of the Levites,” that is, one who is a Levite and in the cities of the Levites redeems by the law of a Levite, and not an Israelite in the cities of the Levites, [that he should] redeem like a Levite.] Rather, say: he redeems only according to this procedure: that we said above, by the law of an Israelite in the cities of Israel.

messages.text: Granted, the house must be from the cities of the Levites, as it is written: “As the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession.” But from where do we derive that the one selling the house must also be a Levite for these halakhot to apply?

verse.he: וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן־הַלְוִיִּם וְיָצָא מִמְכַּר־בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ בַּיֹּבֵל כִּי בָתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הִוא אֲחֻזָּתָם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en: Such property as may be redeemed from Levi—houses sold in a city it holds—shall be released through the jubilee; for the houses in the cities of Levi are its holding among the Israelites.

notes.he: בעינן לאפוקי בן לוי שירש את ישראל כדכתיב ערי הלוים:
notes.en: Granted, the cities of the Levites: we require, to exclude a Levite who inherited from an Israelite, as it is written: “the cities of the Levites.”

notes.he: דבעינן שיהא לוי לאפוקי ישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי:
notes.en: But a Levite, from where do we derive: that we require that he be a Levite, to exclude an Israelite who inherited from his mother’s father, a Levite?

notes.he: אשכחן דאית להו גאולה לעולם ולאו מידי אחרינא דכתיב כי בתי ערי הלוים היא אחוזתם. אבל מנא לן דלוי בערי הלוים דיניה כי האי גוונא ולא איניש אחרינא:
notes.en: Granted, the cities of the Levites: we find that they have a perpetual right of redemption and nothing else, as it is written, “as the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession.” But from where do we derive that a Levite in the cities of the Levites has this law, and no other person?

messages.text: As it is written in the same verse: “And if a man purchases from the Levites…shall go out during the Jubilee Year.” The verse is referring specifically to a Levite who sells his house.

notes.he: דמשמע למקצת לוים נתתי רשות לגאול ולא לכולם:
notes.en: “And if a man purchases from the Levites”: which implies, to some of the Levites I gave permission to redeem, and not to all of them.

notes.he: כלומר לוי שמכר שדהו לישראל יגאל לעולם:
notes.en: As it is written: “And if a man purchases from the Levites”: that is, a Levite who sold his field to an Israelite may redeem it forever.

messages.text: Given that the verse already states: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption” (Leviticus 25:32), why does the next verse state: “And if a man purchases from the Levites…shall go out during the Jubilee Year”? It is because one might have thought: A Levite may always redeem from an Israelite the house that he sold, as this Levite’s power was enhanced, in that he can redeem always, and that Israelite’s power was diminished, as he may redeem only within one year.

notes.he: דדרשינן הכי. ה"ג לה בתורת כהנים מן הלוים מה ת"ל שיכול לוי מישראל יגאל כלומר אי לא כתב אלא גאולת עולם תהיה ללוים יכולני לומר לוי שמכר לישראל יגאלנה לעולם שישראל הורע כחו בממכרו דנחלטת לסוף שנה:
notes.en: And it is taught: that we expound it this way. This is how we read it in Torat Kohanim: “From the Levites,” what does it teach? For one might have thought a Levite may redeem from an Israelite. That is, had it written only “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption,” I could say that a Levite who sold to an Israelite may redeem it forever, since the Israelite’s power is diminished with regard to his sale, in that [his house] becomes [the buyer’s] in perpetuity at the end of a year.

notes.he: לעולם:
notes.en: [One might have thought a Levite may redeem from an Israelite: forever.]

notes.he: בן לוי יפה כחו בממכרו כדמפר' לעיל:
notes.en: As this one: the Levite, his power is enhanced with regard to his sale, as explained above.

messages.text: But a Levite may not always redeem from another Levite, as this one’s power was enhanced and that one’s power was equally enhanced. Rather, the Levite may redeem only within one year of the sale. Therefore, the verse states: “And if a man purchases from the Levites,” which literally means: And if a man redeems from the Levites, which teaches that even a Levite who redeems a house purchased by another Levite can always redeem the house.

notes.he: דכתיב גאולת עולם וגו' אבל לוי שמכר ללוי לא יגאל אלא תיחלט לסוף שנה:
notes.en: And this one’s power is enhanced: as it is written, “a perpetual right of redemption” etc. But a Levite who sold to a Levite may not redeem; rather, it would become [the buyer’s] in perpetuity at the end of a year.

notes.he: פרט לבן לוי שבא מן הממזרת ומן הנתינה וכ"ש ישראל שירש את אבי אמו לוי שהרי ישראל גמור הוא:
notes.en: The verse states: “From the Levites”: to exclude a Levite born of a mamzeret or of a Gibeonite woman; and all the more so an Israelite who inherited from his mother’s father, a Levite, for he is a full Israelite.

notes.he: שמכר ללוי ששניהם יפה כוחם לא יגאל:
notes.en: But a Levite: who sold to a Levite, since the power of both is enhanced, may not redeem.

notes.he: דאפילו לוי מלוי יגאל:
notes.en: The verse states: “From the Levites”: that even a Levite may redeem from a Levite.

messages.text: When the verse states: “From the Levites,” this teaches that some Levites may always redeem their houses, but not all the Levites. Excluded is a Levite who is a son born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzer], or a Gibeonite, i.e., his mother is from the Gibeonites, as these are disqualified from entering the congregation of the Jewish people (see Yevamot 78a). If such a Levite inherited from his father and sold a house from the cities of the Levites, he does not redeem it as a Levite.

notes.he: מן הלוים משמע מעוט כלומר שיש ללוים שאינן בתורת גאולה זו והיינו בן לוי נתין ובן לוי ממזר:
notes.en: “From the Levites,” and not all the Levites: “from the Levites” implies an exclusion, that is, there are Levites who are not under this law of redemption, namely a Levite who is a Gibeonite and a Levite who is a mamzer.

messages.text: But according to the Rabbis, we do not say that the ability to always redeem the house of a Levite does not apply unless the one selling the house will be a Levite. Rather, the Rabbis hold that anyone who inherits a portion in a Levite city may redeem that portion as a Levite, even if he himself is not a Levite.
messages.quote: the Rabbis say: These matters are stated only with regard to a house in the cities of the Levites

notes.he: דלא בעינן תרוייהו) [אבל עד שיהא לוי וערי לוים לא אמרינן דלא בעינן תרוייהו]:
notes.en: (Unless he is a Levite, we do not say: for we do not require both.) [But “unless he is a Levite and the cities of the Levites” we do not say, for we do not require both.]

messages.text: Mishna

The Levites received two thousand cubits surrounding their cities, one thousand cubits of empty lots and one thousand cubits for fields and vineyards. One may neither render a field an empty lot nor an empty lot a field. Similarly, one may neither incorporate an empty lot into a city nor render part of a city an empty lot.

notes.he: מגרש הוי אלף אמה סביב לעיר מדכתיב (במדבר ל״ה:ד׳-ה׳) מקיר העיר וחוצה אלף אמה סביב וחוץ לאותו אלף היה להם ללוים אלף אמה לשדות וכרמים כדכתיב (שם) ומדותם מחוץ לעיר וגו' צא מהם אלף אמה מגרש והשאר שדות וכרמים. מגרש פנוי מכלום ואין בו בית ואין זורעין אותן אלא נוי הוא לעיר:
notes.en: Mishna. A field, a migrash [empty lot]: the migrash is a thousand cubits around the city, from what is written (Numbers 35:4–5): “From the wall of the city and outward a thousand cubits round about.” Beyond that thousand, the Levites had a thousand cubits for fields and vineyards, as it is written: “And you shall measure from outside the city” etc. Take a thousand cubits of migrash from them, and the rest is fields and vineyards. The migrash is empty of everything: there is no house in it and it is not sown; it is a beautification for the city.

notes.he: משום יישוב ארץ ישראל והיינו חורבן שממעט את הזריעה:
notes.en: One may not render a field a migrash: because of the settlement of the Land of Israel; that would be destruction, since it reduces the sowing.

notes.he: שמחריב את נוי העיר:
notes.en: Nor a migrash a field: since he destroys the beauty of the city.

notes.he: שיעשו בו בתים שאין עיר נאה בלא מגרש וכ"ש שאין עושין עיר מגרש שאין מחריבין את יישוב העיר:
notes.en: A migrash one may not make into a city: that they would build houses in it, for a city is not beautiful without a migrash; and all the more so one may not make a city into a migrash, for one does not destroy the settlement of the city.

notes.he: אותן אלף אמה שסביב לעיר שהן אויר לנוי העיר אין עושין אותן שדה שאין זורעין אותן ולא שדה שהוא לזריעה אין עושין אותו מגרש:
notes.en: One may not render a field a migrash: those thousand cubits around the city, which are open space for the city’s beauty, one may not make into a field, for they are not sown; and a field that is for sowing one may not make into a migrash.

messages.text: In what case is this statement said? It applies in the cities of the Levites. But in the cities of the Israelites one may render a field an empty lot but not an empty lot a field, and one may incorporate an empty lot into a city but not render part of a city an empty lot, in order to ensure that they will not thereby destroy the cities of Israel.

notes.he: כדאמר בגמרא לא ישנה:
notes.en: In what case is this statement said? In the cities of the Levites: as it says in the Gemara, “shall not change.”

notes.dh: ולא עיר מגרש שלא יחריבו ערי ישראל
notes.he: שלא יחריב עיר שהיא מיושבת לעשותה מגרש אויר פנוי שלא ישנה [אותה] מכמות שהיא:
notes.en: Nor a city a migrash, so that they will not destroy the cities of Israel: one may not destroy a city that is settled to make it a migrash, empty open space, so that one will not change it from what it is.

messages.text: The priests and the Levites may sell their fields and houses always and may redeem them always, as it is stated: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption.” Priests are also members of the tribe of Levi.

verse.he: וְעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם בָּתֵּי עָרֵי אֲחֻזָּתָם גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם׃
verse.en: As for the cities of Levi, the houses in the cities it holds: Levi shall forever have the right of redemption.

notes.he: אפילו בשנת היובל עצמה כך שמעתי וקשיא לי אמאי הא כי היכי דפליגי רב ושמואל בריש פירקא (לעיל ערכין כט:) בישראל שמכר שדהו בשנת היובל עצמה ה"נ איכא לפלוגי הכא ולמימר ק"ו מכורה כבר יוצאה עכשיו דהא אמרינן לעיל (ערכין דף כח.) דממכרו של לוי חוזר בשנת היובל. וכמדומה לי דאיידי דתנא באידך פירקא מקדישין לעולם וגואלין לעולם תנא נמי הכא:
notes.en: Sell always: even in the Jubilee Year itself; so I heard. But it is difficult for me: why? Just as Rav and Shmuel disagree at the beginning of the chapter (Arakhin 29b) about an Israelite who sold his field in the Jubilee Year itself, so too one could disagree here, and say an a fortiori argument: if what was already sold goes out now, [all the more so what is sold now], for we said above (Arakhin 28a) that a Levite’s sale returns in the Jubilee Year. And it seems to me that since the other chapter taught “they consecrate always and redeem always,” it taught [“sell always”] here too.

notes.he: שאין בתי ערי חומה שלהן נחלטין:
notes.en: Redeem always: for their houses of walled cities do not become [the buyer’s] in perpetuity.

notes.he: אפילו בשנת יובל עצמו:
notes.en: Sell always: even in the Jubilee Year itself.

notes.he: אפילו מיד לאלתר כשמכר:
notes.en: And redeem always: even immediately, as soon as he sold.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that Rabbi Elazar said: In what case is this statement said? It is in the cities of the Levites. But in the cities of the Israelites one may render a field an empty lot but not an empty lot a field, and one may incorporate an empty lot into a city but not render part of a city an empty lot, in order to ensure that they will not thereby destroy the cities of Israel.
messages.quote: In what case is this statement said? It applies in the cities of the Levites

messages.text: In any event, everyone agrees that in the cities of the Levites one may not change a field into an empty lot or an empty lot into a city. From where are these matters derived?

As the verse states: “But the fields of the open land about their cities may not be sold.” What is the meaning of the phrase “may not be sold”? If we say it means that such fields may not be sold at all, that cannot be correct, as from the fact that it is written: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption” (Leviticus 25:32), one learns by inference that their fields may be sold.

verse.he: וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר כִּי־אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם הוּא לָהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: But the unenclosed land about its cities cannot be sold, for that is its holding for all time.

messages.text: Rather, what is the meaning of the phrase “may not be sold”? It means that a field, an empty lot, or a city may not be changed from its current status.

notes.he: מכמות שהיא:
notes.en: Shall not change: from what it is.

messages.text: Why must the verse state: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption”? Since it is stated with regard to the ancestral field of an Israelite: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you,” from which it is derived that one cannot redeem an ancestral field less than two years after its sale, one might have thought that this should also be so with regard to this Levite who sold his field. Therefore, the verse states: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption,” which teaches that a Levite may redeem his field immediately.
messages.lead: § With regard to this halakha, the Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: The priests and the Levites may sell their fields and houses always and may redeem them always

verse.he: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי־תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר־לָךְ׃
verse.en: In buying from your neighbor, you shall deduct only for the number of years since the jubilee; and in selling to you, you shall be charged only for the remaining crop years:

notes.he: לוי כן שאם מכר שדה אחוזתו אותן אלף אמה שחוץ למגרש שלא יהא מותר לגאול בפחות משתי שנים:
notes.en: Gemara. One might have thought that also this one: a Levite, is so: that if he sold his ancestral field, those thousand cubits beyond the migrash, he would not be permitted to redeem it in less than two years.

messages.text: Furthermore, since it is stated: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy unto the Lord, as a field dedicated; his ancestral field shall be for the priest,” one might have thought that this should also be so with regard to this Levite who consecrated his field. Therefore, the verse states: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption,” which teaches that the field of a Levite is not transferred to the possession of the priests in the Jubilee Year; rather, the Levite may always redeem it from the Temple treasury.

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: במקדיש שדה אחוזה וגאלה אחר מיד הקדש דבשנת היובל יוצאה לכהנים כדכתיב והיה השדה וגו':
notes.en: Since it is stated: about one who consecrates an ancestral field and another redeemed it from the Temple treasury, that in the Jubilee Year it goes out to the priests, as it is written: “But the field” etc.

notes.he: לוי כן אם הקדיש שדה ולא גאלה יפסידנה ביובל ת"ל גאולת עולם וגו':
