notes.en: One might have thought that also: a Levite is so, that if he consecrated a field and did not redeem it, he would lose it in the Jubilee. The verse states: “a perpetual right of redemption” etc.

notes.he: ולפי שנאמר קדש לה' כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחוזתו:
notes.en: And since it is stated: “Holy unto the Lord, as a field dedicated; his ancestral field shall be for the priest.”

notes.he: בן לוי שהקדיש את שדהו יוצא לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: One might have thought that also this one is so: that a Levite who consecrated his field, it goes out to the priests in the Jubilee.

messages.text: Additionally, since it is stated: “And if it is not redeemed until the passage of a full year for him, then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity,” one might have thought that this should also be so with regard to this Levite who sold his house in a walled city. Therefore, the verse states: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption,” indicating that the Levite may always redeem his house.

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

messages.text: Granted, with regard to these first two halakhot, which deal with the field of a Levite, it is well. But with regard to the last halakha, why is it necessary for the verse to exclude the houses of Levites? Do Levites have houses of walled cities?
messages.quote: this Levite who sold his house in a walled city

messages.text: With regard to these cities given to the Levites, one does not establish them, neither in small villages nor in large cities; rather, they must be intermediate towns, which are not surrounded by walls.

notes.he: הניתנים ללוים:
notes.en: These cities: those given to the Levites.

notes.he: לפי שהן ערי מקלט ובעינן שיהא שם יישוב לבית מנוס לרוצחים:
notes.en: One does not make them small villages: since they are cities of refuge, and there must be a settlement there to serve as a refuge for killers.

notes.he: לפי שמתקבצין שם מכל מקומות לסחורה ותהא רגל גואל הדם מצויה שם ויארוב את הרוצח ויהרגנו:
notes.en: Nor large cities: since people gather there from everywhere for commerce, and the blood redeemer would often be found there, lie in wait for the killer and kill him.

notes.he: בלא חומה:
notes.en: Rather, intermediate towns: without a wall.

notes.he: של לוים שכתוב ועליהם תתנו ארבעים ושתים עיר:
notes.en: These cities: of the Levites, about which it is written (Numbers 35:6): “And to them you shall add forty-two cities.”

notes.he: כמו מגדלים:
notes.en: Small forts [tirim]: like towers. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads tirim, forts, where the printed Gemara reads kefarim, villages.]

notes.he: שאין מוקפות חומה אלמא לית להו בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: Rather, intermediate towns: that are not surrounded by a wall. Evidently they have no houses of walled cities.

messages.text: This is not difficult. Here, the baraita that states that the cities of the Levites were not surrounded by walls is referring to a city that was initially surrounded by a wall and was ultimately settled. There, the baraita that states that Levites do have houses of walled cities is referring to an intermediate town that was first settled by the Levites and was ultimately surrounded by a wall in the times of Joshua.

notes.he: לא משכחת בהו בלוים כדקאמרת אבל ישב ולבסוף הוקף משכחת בהו שלאחר שניתנו להם בימי יהושע היקיפוה הם:
notes.en: Here, where it was surrounded and ultimately settled: you will not find that with the Levites, as you said. But settled and ultimately surrounded you will find with them, for after the cities were given to them in the days of Joshua, they surrounded them [with a wall].

notes.he: לא קשיא כאן שהוקף חומה ולבסוף ישב שנתנו הם ללוים לית להו [דין] בתי ערי חומה דשוברין חומתן ועושין אותן עיירות בינוניות:
notes.en: It is not difficult: here, where it was surrounded by a wall and ultimately settled, and they gave it to the Levites, they do not have [the law of] houses of walled cities, for they break down their walls and make them intermediate towns. [A gloss in the printed edition suggests the reading: “the Levites do not have it; rather, they would break down their walls” etc.]

notes.he: בלא חומה ונתנוהו ללוים:
notes.en: Here, where it was settled: without a wall, and they gave it to the Levites.

notes.he: שהקיפוהו הלוים מאחר שהיה שלהם יש להם (דין) בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: And ultimately surrounded: the Levites surrounded it after it was theirs; they have the (law of) houses of walled cities.

messages.text: And in a case like this, where the city was first settled and only then surrounded by a wall, is it considered a wall to the extent that the houses inside the city are considered in a walled city?

notes.he: דישב ולבסוף הוקף מי הוי חומה דאצטריך קרא למעוטיה:
notes.en: And in a case like this: settled and ultimately surrounded, is it a wall? A verse was needed to exclude it!

messages.text: The verse states: “And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city.” This is referring to a city that was initially surrounded by a wall and was ultimately settled, and not to a city that was first settled and was ultimately surrounded by a wall.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִמְכֹּר בֵּית־מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ עַד־תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ יָמִים תִּהְיֶה גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who sells a dwelling house in a walled city: It may be redeemed until a year has elapsed since its sale; the redemption period shall be a year.

notes.he: בית שהושב ונבנה עיר חומה דמשמע שהוקף ולבסוף ישב:
notes.en: A dwelling house in a walled city: a house that was settled and built in a walled city, which implies that it was surrounded and ultimately settled.

notes.he: שיהא עיר חומה קודם שיש בה [בית] מושב:
notes.en: A dwelling house in a walled city: it must be a walled city before there is a dwelling [house] in it.

messages.text: One might have thought that it is considered a walled city even if Jews surrounded it with a wall and only then built houses inside it. Therefore, it is stated here: “And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city,” and it is stated below, with regard to the conquest of the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan: “All these were fortified cities, with high walls, gates, and bars.” Just as below, the verse is referring to cities whose surrounding walls were constructed by gentiles, so too here, the verse is referring only to cities whose walls were constructed by gentiles.

verse.he: כׇּל־אֵלֶּה עָרִים בְּצֻרֹת חוֹמָה גְבֹהָה דְּלָתַיִם וּבְרִיחַ לְבַד מֵעָרֵי הַפְּרָזִי הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד׃
verse.en: all those towns were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars—apart from a great number of unwalled towns.

notes.he: לאחר שכבשו את הארץ ואפילו קודם שישבו בה:
notes.en: One might have thought even if Jews surrounded it: after they conquered the land, and even before they settled in it.

notes.he: (דברים ג׳:ה׳) כל אלה ערים בצורות וגו':
notes.en: And it is stated below “wall”: (Deuteronomy 3:5) “All these were fortified cities” etc.

notes.he: חומה ואח"כ ישב יהא לה תורת בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: One might have thought even if Jews surrounded it: with a wall and afterward settled it, it would have the law of houses of walled cities.

notes.he: כל אלה ערים בצורות חומה גבוהה:
notes.en: And it is stated below “wall”: “All these were fortified cities, with high walls.”

notes.he: שהקיפום עובדי כוכבים חומה:
notes.en: Just as below: gentiles surrounded them with a wall.

messages.text: One might have thought that even if gentiles surrounded the city with a wall after the conquest of Eretz Yisrael, it should be considered a walled city. Therefore, it is stated below, with regard to the conquest of the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan, “walls,” and it is stated here “walled.” Just as below, the surrounding walls of the cities were constructed by gentiles before the Jews conquered the land, so too here, the verse is referring to cities whose walls were constructed by gentiles before the conquest of Eretz Yisrael.

notes.he: לאחר שכיבשום ישראל:
notes.en: After that: after the Jews conquered them.

notes.he: בבתי ערי חומה שהקיפום עובדי כוכבים חומה קודם לכן מיכן קודם שירשו ישראל את הארץ]:
notes.en: So too here: with houses of walled cities, gentiles surrounded them with a wall beforehand, that is, before Israel inherited the land.

messages.text: This baraita apparently contradicts the resolution suggested by Rav Kahana, as a city that was first settled and only then surrounded by a wall is not included in the halakhot of houses in walled cities.

Actually, the first baraita is referring to a city that was initially surrounded by a wall and then settled by Levites. And as for the baraita that teaches that Levite cities may not be surrounded by a wall, it is nevertheless possible that a Levite city was initially surrounded by a wall in a case where, when Eretz Yisrael was divided among the tribes of Israel, walled cities fell by lottery to the Levites,
messages.lead: Rav Yosef, son of Rav Sala Ḥasida, interpreted the baraita before Rav Pappa:

notes.he: לעולם כשהוקף ולבסוף ישב ודקשיא לך עיירות הללו אין עושין אותן כו':
notes.en: Rav Sala interpreted it [Rashi’s heading names Rav Sala; the daf reads Rav Yosef, son of Rav Sala Ḥasida]: Actually, where it was surrounded and ultimately settled; and as for what is difficult for you, “these cities one does not make” etc.

notes.he: בגורל בימי יהושע:
notes.en: For example, where they fell to them: by lottery, in the days of Joshua.

notes.he: כלומר כי האי גוונא אפשר למיהוי להו בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: Rav Yosef interpreted it: that is, in a case like this they can have houses of walled cities.

notes.he: ערים בירושה מוקפות חומה מאבי אמו ישראל:
notes.en: Where they fell to them: walled cities, by inheritance from a mother’s father who was an Israelite. [Rashi reads it as falling to them by lottery in the days of Joshua.]

messages.text: Continues on 34a: “…both they and their empty lots.” The Gemara objects that such walls stand to be dismantled, and Rav Ashi explains why the baraita still needed to teach it. A baraita on a priest who consecrates his own dedicated field follows, and on 34a the chapter, and Masechet Arakhin, come to a close.
